papers.title_in_file: Improving Generalization and Trainability of Quantum Eigensolvers via Graph Neural Encoding
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Related Works start, Results opening, Conclusion; did not read the experiment sections or appendices in full.
papers.what_it_is: A graph-autoencoder plus neural-network method that generates VQE parameters across Hamiltonian instances, tested in numerical experiments on spin-model families.

assertions.value: The authors report that, in numerical experiments on families of one- and two-local Hamiltonians, their graph-encoded VQE shows improved generalization and trainability, with reduced test error and a significantly milder decay of gradient variance.
quotes: Through extensive numerical experiments on families of one- and two-local Hamiltonians, we demonstrate improved generalization and trainability, manifested as reduced test error and a significantly milder decay of gradient variance.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study on simulated spin-model families; figures are in the Results section.
assertions.reader_inference: The comparison is against standard VQE and the NNVQE baseline on simulated small systems.

assertions.value: The authors state that EGATE-NNVQE is not meant to be a standalone eigensolver but a high-quality initializer that gives states with enhanced ground-state overlap for unseen instances, to feed downstream routines such as QPE and quantum subspace methods.
quotes: EGATE-NNVQE is not intended to function as a standalone eigensolver capable of producing accurate ground states across an entire Hamiltonian family without adaptation.
it is best viewed as a high-quality initializer that generates initial states with enhanced ground-state overlap for previously unseen instances.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state the intended scope and limit of the method in Section 6, p.13.

assertions.value: The authors report that EGATE-NNVQE initial states, used to warm-start sample-based Krylov quantum diagonalization (SKQD), yield improved convergence under noisy simulation.
quotes: We validated this role by warmstarting SKQD in Sec. 5.1.1, where EGATE-NNVQE initial states yield improved convergence under noisy simulation.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from simulation; the detailed figures were not checked.

assertions.value: The authors state that, to isolate the effect of representation learning, their benchmarks used controlled interaction topologies.
quotes: To isolate the effect of representation learning, our benchmarks focused on controlled interaction topologies.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state the benchmark scope in Section 6, p.13.

papers.title_in_file: Mid-circuit measurement as an algorithmic primitive
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Discussion and Conclusion; did not read the Methods or full Results.
papers.what_it_is: A single-qubit phase-estimation (Hadamard test) feedback scheme that uses mid-circuit measurements to amplify ground-state occupancy, tested in simulation and on IBM hardware.

assertions.value: The authors report that numerical simulations show the method amplifies ground state occupancy, with exponential convergence to optimal states and competitive performance against QAOA using fewer circuit executions.
quotes: Numerical simulations show that this method effectively amplifies the ground state occupancy.
Through simulations, we demonstrated exponential convergence to optimal states and showed competitive performance compared to QAOA with fewer circuit executions.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical simulation results from one study; the QAOA comparison details were not checked.

assertions.value: The authors state that they show mathematically that the desired ancilla outcome biases the state toward the ground space, and that for the undesired outcome the repopulation of low-energy states by a mixer is heuristic.
quotes: We show mathematically that when the ancilla qubit yields the desired outcome, the quantum state is biased towards the ground space in a coherent and systematic way.
When the undesired outcome is obtained, applying a mixer operation heuristically repopulates the low-energy states.
assertions.certainty_reason: Part of the mechanism is argued mathematically; the mixer step is stated to be heuristic, so the whole is not a proof.
assertions.reader_inference: Mixed: one half derived, one half heuristic.

assertions.value: The authors report a hardware validation on a real IBM quantum system, and state that the compiler introduces multiple SWAP gates that increase circuit depth and significantly degrade fidelity.
quotes: We validate our approach on real quantum hardware
the compiler introduces multiple SWAP gates, which increase circuit depth and significantly degrades fidelity.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single hardware experiment; limitation attributed to hardware noise and connectivity.

assertions.value: The authors report that in simulation, selectively protecting the ancilla qubit from noise significantly improves the probability of sampling optimal solutions.
quotes: selectively protecting the ancilla significantly improves the probability of sampling optimal solutions.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical simulation on a small graph instance (Fig. 11).

papers.title_in_file: PQLM - Multilingual Decentralized Portable Quantum Language Model
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Related Work, Methodology, Experiments, Conclusions (whole text read except references).
papers.what_it_is: A quantum LSTM language model whose word embeddings are transferred to a classical sentiment classifier, compared with a classical LSTM.

assertions.value: The authors report that embeddings from the Q-LSTM language model give slightly higher accuracy than those of the classical LSTM and the same weighted f1 score on multilingual Twitter sentiment analysis.
assertions.anchor: Section 4.4, Table 2 (accuracy and f1 values are in the table only), p.3
quotes: The embedding trained by Q-LSTM achieves slightly higher accuracy than the classical LSTM, and has the same weighted f1 score.
Our PQLM exhibits comparable performance to its classical counterpart on both intrinsic evaluation (loss, perplexity) and extrinsic evaluation (multilingual sentiment analysis accuracy) metrics.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-study empirical result on one dataset with a very small model.
assertions.reader_inference: The difference is small and no variance across runs is reported in the text.

assertions.value: The authors state that, given computing constraints, they used only 4 qubits, which gives around 200 parameters for both models, and that the perplexity is not ideal compared to conventional pre-trained language models.
quotes: Given the computing constraints, we only used 4 qubits to train the LSTM model, resulting in an extremely limited number of parameters (around 200) for both models.
Although the model perplexity is not ideal compared to conventional PLMs, it still provides a valuable basis for comparing the classical language model and the PQLM.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state the model size and its limit in Section 4.3.

assertions.value: The authors report that the quantum model converges much faster than the classical model of the same size, while model perplexity for both models is extremely close.
quotes: The PQLM converges much faster than the classical language model of the same size.
Despite the quantum model converging faster than the classical language model, the model quality as measured by model perplexity for both models is extremely close as shown in Table 1.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-study empirical result on one corpus.

assertions.value: The authors claim that the work establishes a theoretical foundation for a portable quantum pre-trained language model that could be trained on private data and released with privacy protection guarantees.
quotes: Our work establishes a theoretical foundation for a portable quantum pre-trained language model that could be trained on private data and made available for public use with privacy protection guarantees.
assertions.certainty_reason: The reading found no privacy experiment or proof in the text; the claim rests on cited work on random circuits.
assertions.reader_inference: Not tested in the paper text read.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum molecular docking with quantum-inspired algorithm
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, results tail and Conclusions; did not read Methods or all Results.
papers.what_it_is: A molecular docking method built on a quantum-annealing-inspired algorithm (hopscotch simulated bifurcation), compared with Autodock Vina and DIFFDOCK.

assertions.value: The authors report that QMD raises the top-1 success rate by about 6% over DIFFDOCK in pocket re-docking, and that QMD with perturbation detection raises the top-1 success rate by about 2% over Autodock Vina in pocket self-docking.
quotes: In pocket re-docking scenario, QMD increases the top-1 success rate of the root-mean-square distance (RMSD) less than
by about 6% compared with DIFFDOCK. In pocket self-docking scenario, QMD with perturbation detection increases the top-1 success rate by about 2% compared with Autodock Vina
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result on one dataset (the DIFFDOCK test set); gains are small.
assertions.reader_inference: The algorithm is quantum-inspired; the quotes do not say it ran on quantum hardware.

assertions.value: The authors state that QMD is based on a quantum-annealing-inspired algorithm, a new simulated bifurcation variant called hopscotch SB (hSB), which can be applied to any objective function under binary variables.
quotes: we propose a novel quantum molecular docking (QMD) approach based on QA-inspired algorithm
This hSB can be applied to any formulation of objective function under binary variables.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors define the method in the Abstract, p.1.

assertions.value: The authors state that generalization of QMD to blind docking is future work.
quotes: In the future, it is also worth studying the generalization of QMD in blind docking scenario.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state the limit in the Conclusions.

assertions.value: The authors report that among the 363 testing protein-ligand pairs, about 65% of QMD predicted docking poses have lower interaction energy than the crystal poses.
quotes: We find that among the 363 testing protein-ligand pairs, about 65% predicted docking poses in QMD have lower interaction energy than the crystal poses.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study; the authors attribute it to the score function, not to docking accuracy.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum machine learning for efficient reduced order modelling of turbulent flows
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Results opening and samples, Discussion, Methods opening; did not read all results sections.
papers.what_it_is: A hybrid quantum-classical reduced-order model (QPOD with quantum deep kernel learning) for turbulent flows, compared with a classical POD-DKL.

assertions.value: The authors report that on benchmark turbulent flows their architecture gives significantly improved predictive accuracy at reduced model ranks, with training speeds up to 10 times faster and parameter counts reduced by a factor of 1/N compared to classical counterparts, where N is the input dimensionality.
quotes: our architecture achieves significantly improved predictive accuracy at reduced model ranks, with training speeds up to 10 times faster and parameter counts reduced by a factor of 1/N compared to classical counterparts, where N is the input dimensionality.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study on three flow cases; speed compares the authors' own implementations.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper names NISQ hardware as a constraint; the quotes do not state where the circuits were run.

assertions.value: The authors state that quantum noise and limited qubit counts currently restrict experimental validation to lower-dimensional regimes, necessitating classical support for high-fidelity flows.
quotes: Key limitations include hardware dependency, where quantum noise and limited qubit counts currently restrict experimental validation to lowerdimensional regimes, necessitating classical support for high-fidelity flows.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state the limit in Section 3 Discussion.

assertions.value: The authors state that the quantum-enhanced DKL used the Adam optimizer with a 4-layer quantum circuit and 300 training epochs, and that fully classical and fully quantum POD-DKL frameworks were compared.
quotes: the Adam optimizer is adopted with a 4-layer quantum circuit, 300 training epochs
fully classical POD-DKL framework and fully quantum POD-DKL framework are compared.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state the setup in Section 4.1.

assertions.value: The authors claim that the framework is poised to surpass classical reduced-order models in speed, accuracy and scalability as hardware matures.
quotes: poised to surpass classical ROMs in speed, accuracy, and scalability as hardware matures
assertions.certainty_reason: A forward-looking claim with no evidence in the paper.

papers.title_in_file: A Novel Hierarchy of Quantum Kernel Networks on Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, selected Results discussion and Concluding Remarks; did not read all numerical sections.
papers.what_it_is: Hybrid quantum-classical networks used as kernels in smoothed particle hydrodynamics, tested on quantum simulators.

assertions.value: The authors report that elementary quantum circuits struggle with generalization in unstructured domains, while the hybrid crossed-QMLP matches the fitting accuracy of classical SPH in quantum optimized space.
quotes: Numerical results show that while elementary quantum circuits struggle with generalization in unstructured domains, the hybrid crossed-QMLP matches the fitting accuracy of classical SPH in quantum optimized space.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study, in simulation.

assertions.value: The authors state that all experiments were run on quantum simulators because of decoherence and gate errors of NISQ devices, and that limitations remain in computational efficiency and hardware implementation.
quotes: Nevertheless, the current study faces limitations in computational efficiency and hardware implementation.
All experiments are conducted on quantum simulators due to the decoherence and gate errors of NISQ devices.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state the limit in Section 5, p.23.

assertions.value: The authors state that accuracy differences among the evaluated networks are marginal, with efficiency the dominant distinguishing factor.
quotes: In practice, the accuracy differences among the evaluated networks are marginal, with efficiency serving as the dominant distinguishing factor.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical observation from one study.

papers.title_in_file: Variational Quantum Algorithm for Constrained Combinatorial Optimization Problems
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Sec. III.B opening, Sec. IV opening, Conclusion; did not read proofs or all result plots.
papers.what_it_is: A variational algorithm with a loss function and a validation oracle for constrained combinatorial optimization, tested on small random graphs.

assertions.value: The authors state that it is provably guaranteed that the loss function's global minimum corresponds uniquely to the optimal feasible solution, because all infeasible solutions get universally higher loss values.
quotes: it is provably guaranteed that its global minimum corresponds uniquely to the optimal feasible solution, as this is achieved by ensuring universally higher loss values for all infeasible solutions.
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 1, Sec. III.B (the proof itself was not read in full).

assertions.value: The authors state that they empirically demonstrate effectiveness on minimum vertex cover and maximum independent set problems on random graphs of varying small-scale sizes.
quotes: we empirically demonstrate its effectiveness by solving minimum vertex cover and maximum independent set problems on random graphs of varying small-scale sizes.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study on small instances.

assertions.value: The authors state that the numerical comparison is against penalty-based methods only, and that a direct comparison with ansatz-based schemes is omitted because of their implementation overhead.
quotes: A direct comparison with ansatz-based schemes is omitted due to their substantial implementation overhead.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state the comparison scope in Section IV.

assertions.value: The authors state that the framework rests on the assumption of an efficient validation oracle, and that this assumption is justified for NPO problems because verifying feasibility is classically efficient.
quotes: Our algorithmic framework is grounded on the assumption of an efficient validation oracle
This assumption is justified for NPO problems, as verifying solution feasibility is classically efficient
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state the assumption in the Introduction.

papers.what_it_is: Quantum optical coherence tomography (quantum sensing) with a theoretical model and a genetic algorithm to infer multilayer sample structure.
papers.why_not: The paper is quantum sensing with entangled photon pairs and a classical genetic algorithm for post-processing; it has no quantum computing or quantum machine learning workload.
